title: A hundred utterances, one writing
literal_meaning: Provisional reading: a hundred utterances, one written record.
explanation: The source places this compact fragment under matter committed to writing. Our reading understands the contrasting term as spoken utterances, but the head does not separately gloss it. The numbers set many beside one; no verb supplies a precise equation or legal rule. We read an invitation to consider what writing preserves, not proof that every written statement is true.
meaning_odia: ଲିଖିତ ବିଷୟ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଉତ୍ସ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଖଣ୍ଡଟି ରଖେ। ଭାକାକୁ ମୁହଁର କଥା ଭାବେ ନେଇ ଆମେ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ ଦେଉଛୁ; ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏଠି ନାହିଁ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଅନେକ ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏକୁ ରଖେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କ୍ରିୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ସମୀକରଣ ବା ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ମିଳେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଲେଖା କଣ ରଖିପାରେ ଭାବେ, ସବୁ ଲେଖା ସତ ବୋଲି ମାନେନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our provisional reading compares speech and writing without inventing a full rule.
odia_summary: ଆମ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ କଥା ଓ ଲେଖାକୁ ତୁଳନା କରେ, ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ନିୟମ ଗଢ଼େନାହିଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନା ପରେ ଦଳଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଥିବା କାମଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଲେଖିଲା ଓ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ି ଶୁଣାଇଲା। / A group writes and checks its agreed tasks together. This application is invented.
cultural_context: Exact ଭାକା and fused ଏକଲେଖା remain unchanged. Other sayings and Krishna Singh literary examples in this long head are separate witnesses, not this fragment’s authorship.
